products.title: Indonesia Bali Subak "Magical" Natural - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Indonesia
Region: Baturiti, Bali
Varietal: Typica, S795
Process: Natural
Altitude: 1,500 - 1,600 MASL
Cupping Notes: Graham, Baking Spices, Plum, Raisin
Recommended Roast: City to Full City+
Good For: Pour Over, Auto Drip, Espresso

Description: Subak is Bali's centuries-old cooperative water system, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape. It's guided by Tri Hita Karana, the Balinese philosophy of harmony between people and nature, with farmers sharing water through canals led by the temples. Coffee grown within this landscape benefits from that same collective care, which helps sustain farming families across the region.

The lot is Typica and S795, grown at 1,500 to 1,600 meters. Typica is one of the oldest arabica varieties around, and S795 is a rust-resistant selection developed in India that's now widely grown in Indonesia.

The standout here is the fermentation. Whole cherries ferment for 72 hours before drying, and that extended fermentation deepens the sweetness and gives the cup its bold flavor and character.

products.title: Indonesia Bali Kintamani Mountain Natural - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Bali
Region: Kintamani, Bali
Varietal: Kate Kartika, B-1
Process: Natural
Altitude: 1,300 - 1,600 MASL
Cupping Notes: Apple, Dates, Honey
Recommended Roast: City to Full City+
Good For: Pour Over, Auto Drip, Espresso

Description: Farmers in the Kintamani Highlands originally grew citrus as their main crop. Over time they started planting coffee in between the citrus trees to get more out of their land, and since both crops shared the same fertilization, the coffee did well. It gradually became a primary source of income, supporting farming families across the region.

The washing station buys coffee cherries directly from local farmers and processes them into specialty, export-ready coffee. This lot is a natural, and the key to its quality is a carefully controlled fermentation that shapes the flavor and character of the cup.The varieties are B-1 and Kate Kartika, grown at 1,300 to 1,600 meters. Kartika is a compact dwarf type of Catuaí, and the "kate" in the name is derived from the local word for dwarf.

products.title: Peru Amazonas - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Peru
Region: Bagua Grande
Varietal: Caturra, Typica
Process: Washed
Altitude: 1,300 - 1,900 MASL
Cupping Notes: Graham Cracker, Plum, Milk Chocolate
Recommended Roast: City to Full City
Good For: Auto Drip, Pour Over, Espresso, Blends

Description: Bagua Grande is located in the province of Uctubamba, department of Amazonas in northeastern Peru. Amazonas, like much of Peru, is renowned for natural beauty, from a wide variety of tropical birds to the Yumbilla and Gocta waterfalls. The region has the ideal elevation and climate for producing high scoring specialty coffee. Farmers in this region traditionally used slash and burn techniques which would quickly embed nutrients into the soil, but also resulted in deforestation of forests. Today, coffee farmers are working to reverse the deforestation through agroforestry models in coffee and cacao production. The bulk of the coffee exported from Amazonas is produced on smallholder farms where they handle everything from harvest to processing and drying. Cooperatives here function mainly as dry mills, hulling the parchment from dried coffee, and warehouses where coffee is prepped for export.

products.title: Mexico Finca Las Chicharras Washed - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Mexico
Region: Motozintla, Chiapas
Varietal: Bourbon, Caturra, Marsellesa, Maragogype
Farm: Finca Las Chicharras
Process: Washed 
Altitude: 1,250 - 1,600 MASL
Cupping Notes: Brown Sugar, Plum, Almond
Recommended Roast: City to Full City
Good For: Pour Over, Auto Drip, Full Immersion, Espresso, Blends

Description: Finca Las Chicharras (“Cicada” in English) took 5th in the Cup Of Excellence competition in Mexico 2018, and it’s no surprise when cupping coffee from the farm. This is quite a feat for E-Cafe Chiapas, the operation who runs the farm. They began as an exporter in 2007, with their first container shipping to the US, built a processing plant in 2013, and didn’t purchase their own finca until 2015 — that farm was Finca Las Chicharras. It’s an insane timeframe, to go from first time farm owner to COE winner in the span of 3 years. The group is not only mastering coffee production, they also have in place many social programs to improve the lives of people who work with them, or live in the surrounding areas. Their main operations outside of coffee are the Icathus School, a boarding school for underprivileged children, affordable financing offered to producers, and working with community and government leaders to improve infrastructure, education, and health. These operations are funded by the government and the sales of their coffee. Finca Las Chicharras operates not only as an award winning coffee farm for E-Cafe, but also as a research and development facility where all farmers who work with the group are invited to learn how to improve their own practices.

This handpicked lot is sent to the fermentation tanks for 10-14 hours before being washed clean of mucilage. After it’s been washed the coffee is sorted and then put on raised beds in a greenhouse for drying that maintains a temperature of 30-35℃. The coffee will go through destoning next to ensure no foreign matter makes it through the process, and then the coffee is hulled to remove the parchment. With the coffee processed down to green coffee, E-Cafe runs it through a color sorter, and finishes with size grading to be sure that the resulting coffee is uniform and without defects for the best quality across the lot.

Finca Las Chicharras is a beautiful farm and produces some beautiful coffees, this one cups almost Kenya-like with its bright acidity.

products.title: Mexico El Mezcal - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Mexico
Region: Chiapas
Varietal: Bourbon, Catuai, Arabe
Process: Washed 
Altitude: 1,250 - 1,600 MASL
Cupping Notes: Brown Sugar, Lime, Dark Chocolate
Recommended Roast: City to Full City
Good For: Pour Over, Auto Drip, Full Immersion, Espresso

Description: El Mezcal is a beautiful example of the specialty coffee industry taking small scale producers from selling on local markets to being represented for their own individual quality. E-Cafe Chiapas is an organization of growers who started out as an exporter in 2007. They organize this microlot that is produced by 12 small scale growers who had previously sold their coffee into a larger regional blend. E-Cafe hosted the farmers who contribute to El Mezcal at their research farm, Finca Las Chicharras, in 2016 to learn growing and processing techniques for specialty coffee. Then in 2019, the E-Cafe team helped El Mezcal build their own raised beds for drying coffee, as they were previously drying it in their yards. Before getting into the processing and cup profile for this lot, we have to touch on the epic name, “El Mezcal”. Unfortunately it was not named because these 12 producers got together, sang songs, and drank mezcal all night. Last year was our first year bringing in this microlot, and we actually misunderstood where they name came from. On a visit to Chiapas in early 2022, we learned the name comes from a tree called “Mezcal”.  In all honesty I cannot find this tree on the internet so there must be another name for it, but it’s an impressively large shade giving tree (size-wise, think a canopied redwood).

This handpicked lot is sent to the fermentation tanks for 24 hours before being washed clean of mucilage. After it’s been washed the coffee is sorted and then put on raised beds in a greenhouse for drying that maintains a temperature of 30-35℃. The coffee will go through destoning next to ensure no foreign matter makes it through the process, and then the coffee is hulled to remove the parchment. With the coffee processed down to green coffee, E-Cafe runs it through a color sorter, and finishes with size grading to be sure that the resulting coffee is uniform and without defects for the best quality across the lot.

products.title: Ethiopia Gori Gesha Double Anaerobic Natural Gr1 - Green
products.body_html:
Country: Ethiopia
Region: Gesha, SNNPR
Varietal: Gori Gesha & Gesha 1931
Process: Natural + Double Anaerobic
Altitude: 1,400 - 1,684 MASL
Cupping Notes: Cherry Cordial, Rosé, Vanilla
Recommended Roast: City to Full City
Good For: Pour Over, Auto Drip, Espresso

Description: Established in 2019, this Gesha region farm is lesser known compared to Yirgacheffe or Guji, but its varieties are exceptional. The famed Gesha 1931 and its sibling, Gori Gesha—one of the oldest known coffee varieties—originate from the nearby Gori Gesha Forest, just 20 minutes from the farm.

Owned by our export partner, the farm tightly controls picking and processing, producing everything from anaerobics and carbonic macerations to traditional naturals. This lot went through a double anaerobic: 48 hours of sealed fermentation, 24 hours of shade drying, then a second 72-hour ferment before finishing 17 days on raised beds. The break between ferments builds complexity without pushing the coffee into heavy, boozy territory. Thanks to the region's warm climate, naturals develop beautifully here.

One of several sister lots from this farm—each a different ferment on the same cherry—this coffee is vibrant, fruity, and truly distinctive; perfect if you're seeking something uncommon.
